restore

/ri-STOR/ — stress on STOR · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To restore something is to repair it and bring it back to its original, good condition.

The bookbinder restored the crumbling atlas, resewing its spine and flattening its brittle pages.

Example

The town restored its century-old carousel over two summers, tracking down the original blueprints and hand-carving new horses to match the ones from 1910.

Restore = re (again) + staurare (Latin: to set up) = to set it up again. The town isn't just fixing a worn-out ride — it's returning the carousel to its original condition, right down to the 1910 horses. That specificity makes restore far more precise than the plain word repair.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

renovate: To renovate is to update and modernize a building — a new kitchen, new wiring, a brighter open layout. To restore aims the opposite way: returning a thing to its original condition. A renovated theater gets modern seats and screens; a restored theater gets its 1920s gilding back.

rehabilitate: To rehabilitate is to bring someone or something back to health or usefulness — an injured athlete, a polluted river, a rundown neighborhood. To restore is about condition and appearance, returning a thing to its original state. Rehabilitation asks whether it works again; restore asks whether it is as it originally was.

refurbish: To refurbish is to clean, brighten, and spruce something up, often so it can be used or sold again — fresh paint, new upholstery. To restore sets a stricter goal: bringing the piece back to its exact original condition, matching what the maker first produced rather than simply making it presentable.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

damage: harm something so it no longer works well

ruin: destroy something beyond repair or usefulness

Where it sits · how fully it returns to original condition

patch → fix → repair → restore

patch vs. restore: You might patch a leaky roof to get through one storm, but to restore the whole house is to return it to its original glory.

fix vs. restore: Fixing a wobbly chair leg takes ten minutes, while restoring an antique chair to its original condition can take months of careful work.

repair vs. restore: A mechanic can repair the engine so it runs, but only a specialist can fully restore a classic car to gleaming showroom condition.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-: again (Latin)

Root — store: to set up, make firm (from Latin staurare)

Put it together: Re- (again) + store (to set up, make firm — from Latin staurare) literally means 'to set something up again' — to bring a thing back to the good, solid condition it once had.

Use the root in a new word: restaurant: A restaurant was originally named as a place that 'restored' weary travelers — after the long hike, we stopped at a small restaurant to refuel.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Reach for restore when something broken or neglected is being fixed and returned to its original good condition. For routine repairs, repair is simpler. For updates that improve beyond the original, renovate is clearer.
